title: cost-optimization-autotune-defaults-batching-caching-quant-uecon-tooling
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: reduce per-token unit cost for common production workloads by providing safer, conservative defaults and automation for batching, KV caching, and quantization profiles, plus adding unit-economics (uecon) tooling to surface expected cost impact to customers and internal dashboards. This PR bundles three coordinated efforts: 1) Autotune defaults for batching and caching based on observed latency/throughput distributions; 2) Production-ready quantization profiles with validation and a fall-back path; 3) Unit economics endpoints and Console integration for model-config cost estimation.

Summary of changes (single continuous description): Added an autotune controller that computes conservative default batch sizes and caching TTLs from historical p50/p95 sequence length and QPS distributions; extended the runtime scheduler to accept autotune hints and optionally enforce per-customer pinned defaults; introduced a quantization profile registry (profiles/*.yaml) and validation logic that verifies accuracy drop thresholds (regression <= 1.5% by configured eval suites) before allowing automatic promotion; added a uecon service and new /v1/uecon/estimate endpoint that returns token-cost estimates for a given model+config and synthetic traffic pattern; Console: added a per-model cost-preview panel and rollout toggle for enabling autotuned defaults; docs + SDK: typescript & python examples for calling the uecon endpoint; tests & safety: regression eval jobs for quant profiles and canary rollout plan.

Checklist: 
- [x] Autotune controller implementation and unit tests
- [x] Runtime integration and end-to-end perf tests
- [x] Quant profiles + regression eval harness
- [x] uecon API + Console integration
- [x] Feature flag + canary rollout plan
- [x] Release notes and migration guidance

Rollout plan: feature-flagged on by default in staging for 48h; canary rollout to 5% of traffic for 72h with automatic rollback on latency or quality regressions (>5% latency p95 or >1.5% decrease in eval pass rate). Full rollout after manual QA and SRE signoff.

Notes: This PR intentionally chooses conservative defaults (smaller batch multipliers and shorter cache TTLs) to prioritize latency SLOs. The autotune controller will suggest more aggressive configurations as confidence increases. The uecon endpoint is read-only and no customer traffic is changed without explicit rollout toggles.
commits_summary: 7 commits: initial autotune controller; integrate autoscheduler hints; add quantization profile registry and validation; implement /v1/uecon/estimate; console: cost-preview panel and toggle; tests: add regression evals and perf canary; docs + SDK examples.
review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Please add a safety check in the scheduler to avoid growing batch size above 1.5x observed optimal at p95. Added in commit 4.
Maya Chen: Quant profile evals look good, but we need to ensure the eval suite runs in CI nightly. Author: added nightly job and annotated the YAML.
Rajat Singh: Can we make uecon estimates use spot-pricing and reserved-pricing models? Author: added pricing-mode param and documented fallback behavior.
SRE (Sharon Park): Add alerting thresholds for canary rollback on latency/queue-growth. Author: added SLO-based metrics and an alerting playbook.
QA (Diego Morales): Console UX needs clearer callout when defaults are autotuned vs user-pinned. Author: UI update in CostPreviewPanel to show badge.
Author reply: Addressed comments; split heavy work into feature-flagged components to shorten rollout and reduce blast radius.

e2e perf canary: pass on staging (p50/p95 latency within SLO)
regression evals: pass for all promoted quant profiles
release_notes:
- Add autotune defaults for batching and caching to reduce unit cost while preserving latency SLOs.
- Introduce quantization profile registry with validation and safe promotion.
- Expose /v1/uecon/estimate to preview cost impact of model/config choices in Console and SDKs.
- Feature-flagged rollout with canary and automatic rollback on regressions.
risk_assessment: Medium: changes touch runtime scheduler and quantization promotion paths. Mitigations: feature flags, canary rollout, conservative defaults, nightly regression evals, and automatic rollback on SLO/quality regressions.
notes_for_release: Ops: enable feature flag 'autotune_defaults' in staging for validation, then canary 5% production. Engineering: monitor uecon dashboard and /metrics/autotune_suggestions. Security: no new data plane access; no PII changes.
